name: Abd Yaghuth al-Harithi
bio: Abd Yaghuth ibn Sala'a, or by another account ibn al-Harith ibn Waqqas ibn Sala'a, was a pre-Islamic poet of the Yemeni tribe of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, part of Madhhij; Abu al-Faraj calls him a horseman and chief of his people, who led them against Tamim at the Second Day of al-Kulab. Poetry ran in his family before and after Islam: its poets included his grandsons al-Lajlaj and Mushir, the horseman who put out the eye of Amir ibn al-Tufayl at Fayf al-Rih, and, in Islamic times, Ja'far ibn Ulba. When Madhhij was routed at al-Kulab he was taken prisoner, and Taym al-Ribab insisted on killing him for their own chief, al-Nu'man ibn Jisas; Ibn Rashiq says they refused a ransom of a thousand camels. Abu al-Faraj says they gave him wine and cut the great vein of his forearm, Ibn Habib that they beheaded him; al-Zirikli puts his death around 40 years before the Hijra (around 584 CE), though Abu al-Faraj places al-Kulab after the Persian blow to Tamim at al-Mushaqqar, which Lyall dates to about 611 CE. The poem he made as a captive, “Ala la talumani”, is the thirtieth of al-Mufaddaliyyat.
